evals.prompt: Build an eval framework for us. We have an AI feature that generates marketing email subject lines and preview text from a campaign brief (audience, offer, tone guidelines, key message). This goes out to real customers — some sends are reviewed by a marketer first, but we're moving toward letting some segments send unreviewed. Known problems so far: subject lines sometimes overstate the offer (calling a 10% discount 'huge savings'), and the tone drifts off-brand when the brief is thin. We don't have any eval process today.
evals.expected_output: A full framework with 4-6 dimensions specific to subject lines/preview text (should include something like instruction adherence/offer accuracy and tone/brand fit given the stated failure modes), a 1-5 rubric with concrete anchors per dimension, a golden set structure with category proportions, and explicit pass/fail thresholds that treat overstated-offer as a hard-fail given it's customer-facing and moving toward unreviewed sends.
expectations: At least one dimension directly addresses factual/offer accuracy, tied to the known 'overstates the offer' failure mode
At least one dimension addresses tone/brand fit, tied to the known tone-drift failure mode
Rubric anchors are specific to subject lines/preview text, not generic 1-5 quality language
Golden set structure includes the six standard categories (typical, edge case, known failure modes, adversarial, ambiguous, out-of-scope) or explains why one is omitted
Known failure modes category explicitly includes cases built from the overstatement and tone-drift problems
Pass/fail thresholds are concrete and checkable, not vague
Offer accuracy or a comparable correctness dimension is flagged as a hard-fail dimension given customer-facing, moving-to-unreviewed context
Judge prompt is offered, not force-generated
Open assumptions are noted since no existing eval process exists

evals.prompt: We built an internal tool that summarizes long customer support threads for our support agents before they respond. Agents always read the original thread if something looks off, so this is a lower-stakes internal aid, not customer-facing. We want an eval framework so we can compare two different prompt versions.
evals.expected_output: A framework calibrated for a lower-stakes, human-reviewed, internal use case — dimensions likely include correctness/grounding and completeness, but thresholds should be less strict than a customer-facing example, and the framework should be usable for A/B comparing two prompt versions specifically.
expectations: Dimensions are relevant to summarization specifically (e.g., grounding/faithfulness to the source thread, completeness of key points, actionability for the agent)
The framework explicitly reflects that this is lower-stakes/human-reviewed by calibrating thresholds less strictly than a customer-facing feature would warrant
Golden set guidance addresses that this framework will be used to compare two prompt versions (e.g., running the same golden set against both)
Thresholds are still concrete and checkable, not just 'less strict' without specifics
Hard-fail dimensions, if any, are limited given the human-in-the-loop safety net (not over-applying safety strictness meant for unreviewed customer-facing output)
Judge prompt offer is made

evals.prompt: Build me an eval framework for our AI-generated product descriptions on our e-commerce site, and go ahead and give me the judge prompt too so I can start automating scoring right away.
evals.expected_output: A full framework, and since the judge prompt was explicitly requested up front, it should be included in the same response rather than offered and held back for a follow-up.
expectations: Full framework delivered: dimensions, rubric with anchors, golden set structure, thresholds
Judge prompt is generated directly in this response since it was explicitly pre-requested, not just offered
Judge prompt incorporates the actual rubric anchors from the framework, not a generic scoring prompt
Judge prompt specifies a structured output format for aggregation
A caveat is included that the judge prompt needs periodic spot-checking against human scores
Dimensions are specific to product descriptions (e.g., factual accuracy about the product, compliance with required disclosures, tone)
